title: Shunga Empire
capsule: The Shunga Empire was founded circa 185 BCE when the Brahmin general Pushyamitra Shunga assassinated the last Mauryan emperor, Brihadratha, and seized control of Magadha. At its height the empire controlled much of northern and central India, including the Ganges valley, Malwa, and parts of the Deccan, though it steadily lost territory to the expanding Satavahana kingdom in the south and to Greek Indo-Bactrian incursions in the northwest—the Menander-era campaign reaching as far as Pataliputra, according to Patañjali. Patronage of Sanskrit literature and Hindu religious art flourished under the Shungas, who commissioned the celebrated gateways (toranas) of the Sanchi stupa. The empire fragmented around 73 BCE when its last ruler, Devabhuti, was overthrown by the minister Vasudeva Kanva.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Shunga territorial extent is reconstructed from inscriptions, numismatics, and textual sources; precise boundaries, particularly in the northwest and south, are debated among scholars.
